key_insight: A recurrent automatic speech recognition (ASR) system mirrors the human auditory cortex: distinct model layers map to distinct cortical regions and together form a parallel hierarchical progression from acoustic features to phonetic, lexical and semantic representations.
problem_solved: Clarifies whether and how layered representations in engineered ASR systems correspond to the spatial and representational hierarchy of speech processing in the human brain, bridging model interpretability and neural organization.
method: Record neural responses from human auditory cortex during natural speech perception and extract time-aligned neural activation patterns.
Compute layerwise representations from a recurrent ASR system and use representational-alignment/encoding analyses to map model layers onto cortical sites.
Characterize the informational content at each layer and cortical region to show a parallel progression (acoustic → phonetic → lexical → semantic).
impact: Provides strong evidence that modern recurrent ASR models reproduce brain-like, spatially distributed language encoding — useful for interpretable, brain-inspired model design and for using models as hypotheses in cognitive neuroscience. This alignment can guide architecture choices and diagnostics in speech systems.
visual_elements: Cortical surface map annotated with colored links from model layers to corresponding auditory regions (layer → region mapping).
Layer-stack diagram showing progression of representations (acoustic → phonetic → lexical → semantic) alongside example activations.
Heatmap or matrix of representational similarity / alignment scores between model layers and recording sites.
Timeline plot illustrating how different linguistic contents emerge over time in both model activations and neural responses.
paper_title: Parallel hierarchical encoding of linguistic representations in the human auditory cortex and recurrent automatic speech recognition systems
paper_authors: Menoua Keshishian, Gavin Mischler, Samuel Thomas, Brian Kingsbury, Stephan Bickel
